judged_text: The delete action attaches only .then to destroyRecord() with no rejection handler, unlike save() which pairs its promise with .catch(popupAjaxError), so a failed host deletion produces no error surface at all. When the DELETE fails (network error, or the 500 the destroy action returns for an already-deleted id on a double-delete), the admin gets no popup and no indication of failure — the row silently remains in the table and the operation looks like it did nothing.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` but never attaches a rejection handler (unlike `save()`, which does `.catch(popupAjaxError)`). If the DELETE fails, the UI provides no error feedback and the host is not removed (because `deleteHost` is only sent in the `.then`). This is especially plausible given `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy` does `host = ...first; host.destroy` without a nil check, so a missing/already-deleted id would raise and return a 500.
